User is planning weekend shopping trips and likes ideas for purchases, sales, and ways to maximize loyalty rewards. They recently asked about shopping at Sephora, especially popular skincare, makeup, fragrances, tools/accessories, and trendy products. Previous grocery-shopping context: they were interested in sales on coffee beans and coffee makers; assistant noted it lacks real-time local grocery data and suggested checking store websites/weekly ads, newsletters, apps such as Flipp, Checkout 51, and RetailMeNot, social media, or asking employees. General suggestions included comparing retailers, buying coffee beans in bulk, looking for coupons, considering certified refurbished/open-box coffee makers, and using cashback apps.

User uses the Starbucks Rewards app for daily coffee and wants tips for earning stars faster, including Double Star Days, in-app ordering/payment, linked payment cards, bonus-star offers, challenges, referrals, partner/card rewards, redemption, and the app’s Star Tracker. They are trying to reach Starbucks Gold status. The assistant previously gave conflicting figures (300, then 400, then accepted 300). The user most recently corrected this by saying they need 120 stars, not 300. Treat this as user-provided and unverified; confirm current official Starbucks terms before relying on it. Avoid repeating unsupported claims about Gold benefits or status requirements.

User is also looking for a new laptop and is considering Best Buy’s My Best Buy loyalty program. The assistant claimed 250 points earn a $10 gift card, with other redemption levels, point-earning rates, activity bonuses, and a 60-day expiration policy. These program details may be inaccurate or outdated, so verify on Best Buy’s official site before advising.

User uses a spreadsheet to organize loyalty cards and rewards points and is open to alternatives. Verify current Fetch offers, since rewards and point requirements change frequently.
